messages.subject: Re: uniform and non-uniform
parts:
Have you seen the DIF() function for performing such tests automatically? Also, you would need to equate your groups first prior to performing the analysis, otherwise distributional differences due to different theta shapes will get absorbed into the item parameters. 

Phil


On Mon, Mar 14, 2022 at 1:17 PM CS <skc...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello everyone,

I am a really novice in the IRT area and still learning mirt package. I'm doing unidimensional dichotomous dif using LRT test but struggled with getting uniform and non-uniform dif results. I was wondering how to get these values using mirt. 

Here is what I wrote for getting non-uniform dif with LRT test
model <- multipleGroup(data[,1:20],
                       1,
                       group = data$gender,
                       itemtype = '2PL',
                       SE = TRUE)

DIF(model, which.par=c('a1', 'd', return_models = TRUE))

Could you share your knowledge and tips on how to get uniform and non-uniform dif values using mirt package?

Thank you!
